title: TensorPlate Backend Descriptor
description: Metadata file installed by an out-of-tree backend package (e.g. `tensorplate-backend-python-pytorch`). The agent + CLI use this descriptor to detect backend presence, version compatibility, interpreter compatibility, runtime availability, and the sidecar entrypoint without executing user model code. Lives under `/usr/share/tensorplate/backends/<backend_name>/backend.json` after install.

backend_name.description: Stable identifier the bundle's `backend_hint` matches against (e.g. `python_pytorch`, `tensorrt`, `libtorch`).

package_name.description: OS-level package name. Used by `tensorplate doctor` in install hints.

package_version.description: Backend package version (PEP 440 or Debian-style). Reported by `doctor` and compared against `tensorplate_runtime_range`.

tensorplate_runtime_range.description: TensorPlate runtime versions this backend is known compatible with. The agent rejects the deploy at compatibility time when the runtime version is outside this range.

interpreter.description: Absolute path to the Python interpreter the sidecar must invoke. Optional; when absent the runtime falls back to `python3` from PATH.

import_module.description: Module the sidecar imports at startup. Detection probes verify this is importable without executing user model code.

capabilities.description: Capability flags published by this backend. The agent verifier checks bundle `capability_requirements` against this declaration; missing fields default to all-false / empty.

install_hint.description: Human-readable hint reported by `tensorplate doctor` when the backend is missing or unrunnable.
